problem: "The leading edge may be fixed and the trailing edge shifted, or the reverse" describes PWM, not PPM. In PPM the width stays fixed and the whole narrow pulse slides in time.
fix: PPM keeps height and width fixed and slides the whole pulse earlier or later about its nominal slot by an amount proportional to m(t). (Fixed one edge with a moving other edge is PWM.)

where: Section 2, PPM generation, and Quiz Q5
problem: An edge detector giving "one short pulse per PWM edge" produces two pulses per PWM period, so the pulse rate doubles and the modulation is not the standard PPM. PPM has one pulse per sampling period.
fix: Take one edge per PWM period, usually the modulated trailing edge, and let a monostable or differentiator-plus-rectifier turn it into one short pulse: "one short pulse per PWM period, produced at the modulated edge".

problem: "This keeps the pulse timing fixed" contradicts PPM, where the pulse position is the message.
fix: Say that the pulse period Ts stays fixed and only one pulse parameter (height, width or position) carries the message.

problem: The formula P_PAM(f) = (1/Ts) Σ M(f − n fs)·P(f) with P(f) = Aτ sinc(fτ) is the flat-top (sample-and-hold) PAM result. It is stated as the general PAM spectrum even though natural PAM was just defined.
fix: Label it as the flat-top PAM spectrum. For natural PAM the spectrum is Σ c_n M(f − n fs) with c_n = (τ/Ts) sinc(n τ/Ts), a weighted set of replicas, not M(f) multiplied by P(f).

problem: Powers of ten appear as plain digits: "8×103 Hz", "125×10−6 s", "10×103". Read literally these are wrong values (8×103 = 824), which confuses a phone reader.
fix: Write 8×10<sup>3</sup> Hz, 125×10<sup>−6</sup> s (125 μs), 10×10<sup>3</sup> Hz, and 25×10<sup>−6</sup> s.

problem: "Some syllabi call PPM pulse-position modulation and PWM pulse-duration modulation" repeats names already defined one paragraph earlier (PDM was introduced as the same thing as PWM).
fix: Delete the sentence, or place the PDM/PWM synonym note at the first mention and add the point that a few texts separate pulse-duration modulation (one edge fixed) from pulse-width modulation (both edges move).
